significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that subliminal traits obey a specific intervention ordering—"any small random subset" has little effect, "targeted removal of a low-rank trait subspace removes it efficiently," and compression preserves them better than matched overt traits—making this a form-(iii) relation among measurable ablation, compression, and behavioral-retention quantities. It would establish both a phenomenon (differential robustness) and a mechanism-level storage geometry (low-dimensional yet distributed), fixing expectations for several interventions rather than merely locating a trait; this distinction matters because Hase et al. (2023), Does Localization Inform Editing?, shows that localization alone does not guarantee editability. The branches are determinate and informative: failure of the random-versus-targeted ordering would reject the proposed distributed-low-rank account, while matched subliminal/overt curves would undercut the claimed difference in how covert and explicit training write traits. In the topic-substitution check, merely proposing to extend subliminal learning would not earn this score; the added cross-intervention ordering and matched-training comparison are what place it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is "targeted removal of a low-rank trait subspace," supplemented by the claimed "rank/parameter budget needed to remove the trait"; this is an actionable post-training intervention rather than merely an explanatory description. Once a trait direction is identified, it can be applied before deployment and therefore offers lead time against behavioral manifestation, with model auditors and deployers as plausible downstream users, although it is not an ex-ante detector of an unknown trait. After re-extraction on another model, the hypothesis predicts the qualitative relation—random removal should be weak while targeted low-rank removal is efficient—rather than supplying only an open-ended search procedure, but it does not expressly claim invariance across architectures, scales, or quantization implementations. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: "extend subliminal learning" supplies neither this mitigation handle nor the transferable intervention ordering.
